_comment: Authoritative CORE/ADAPTER/COUPLED classification and per-path vendor-coupling allowances, enforced by scripts/check-vendor-coupling.sh. THIS JSON is the single source of truth the gate reads; the gate hard-codes no token, no glob and no allowance, so every policy change is a reviewable diff here. RATCHET SEMANTICS: breach = actual > allowance; actual < allowance PASSES (debt paid down is never a CI failure). To add a reference to a ratcheted path, raise its allowance in the SAME PR, which puts the raise in front of a reviewer — the same convention prompt-token-budgets.json uses for prompt budgets. COUNTING: the gate counts LITERAL fixed-string occurrences of `vendor_tokens` per tracked file (git ls-files + grep -oF), summing all tokens and counting every occurrence, not every matching line — a line-based count would let a second reference hide on an existing line. HONEST LIMIT: a reference ASSEMBLED AT RUNTIME (built by concatenation or indirection) contains no literal token and is invisible to this mechanism; a green run means 'no new LITERAL coupling', not 'no new coupling'. SCOPE LIMIT: only `scan_roots` is scanned. Root prose (README.md, CLAUDE.md, CHANGELOG.md), the sibling plugins (stackpack/, mysql-mcp/) and .github/ are deliberately UNSCANNED, not certified clean — release prose names the harness by necessity and would force an allowance bump every release, which is how a gate earns being switched off. REFUTED ASSUMPTION, recorded on purpose: the source requirement assumed these references 'are dominated by legitimately-adapter surfaces (commands/hooks/agent frontmatter)'. Measured on the base commit of this change, adapter-ish surfaces were 131/278 = 47% and core-ish surfaces 139/278 = 50% — the assumption is REFUTED; adapter surfaces are NOT dominant. The mitigating fact is that the CORE allowance table is nonetheless small, so ratcheting it down later is tractable. (Those 278/131/139 figures are MATCHING-LINE counts from the requirement's own measurement, kept verbatim as the historical record; this gate counts OCCURRENCES, which are >= line counts, so the numbers below are legitimately larger.) The allowance values below were produced by `bash scripts/check-vendor-coupling.sh --print-allowances` and committed as measured — never hand-typed.
unclassified_default_note: A path matched by no class glob is treated as CORE with an allowance of 0, so a brand-new directory cannot silently become a coupling haven: the first vendor reference added to it fails CI until someone classifies it here. The gate rejects `adapter` as a default outright — a blanket adapter default would exempt the entire tree and make the ratchet vacuous.
glob_syntax_note: Globs are shell `case` patterns evaluated against the repo-relative path, where `*` DOES match `/`. So `loomwright/skills/*` covers the whole subtree, and no `**` form is needed. ADAPTER is matched first, then COUPLED, then CORE — which is what lets a single-file adapter exemption win over the broader CORE glob that contains it.

adapter.note: Adapter surfaces may name any harness freely and are NOT counted at all. loomwright/commands, loomwright/agents and loomwright/hooks are prompt/manifest surfaces the harness itself parses — they exist to speak Claude Code's language, and demanding neutrality from them would be demanding they stop working. The two .claude-plugin MANIFESTS (.claude-plugin/marketplace.json and loomwright/.claude-plugin/plugin.json) are literally the vendor's packaging format, and are named individually rather than by a directory glob ON PURPOSE: a `.claude-plugin/*` glob also swept in .claude-plugin/README.md, which is prose rather than a manifest, silently exempting its references while this note claimed to be exempting only manifests. That prose file is now COUPLED and ratcheted like any other doc. loomwright/scripts/resolve-loomwright-root.sh is exempt DELIBERATELY and load-bearingly: its entire job is to name the harness variable ONCE so that nothing else has to, and a gate that flagged it would be flagging the seam that exists to remove the coupling everywhere else.

coupled.note: Grandfathered debt. loomwright/skills and loomwright/docs carry real, already-paid-for coupling: skills document harness-specific workflows and docs describe the harness by name. They are ratcheted exactly like CORE — the allowance simply starts from a higher measured baseline. Classifying them COUPLED rather than ADAPTER is the point: an adapter exemption would never be paid down, whereas a COUPLED allowance can only fall. .claude-plugin/README.md is listed explicitly for the reason given in the adapter note: it is prose that sits in a manifest directory, so it is classified by what it IS, not by where it lives.

core.note: The portable core: the plugin's runtime shell/python scripts. These are the files a non-Claude adapter would have to run unmodified, so every literal harness reference in them is a porting cost. 35 files under loomwright/scripts currently carry references and therefore hold an allowance entry; every other file's allowance is 0, which is precisely what makes a NEW reference in a currently-clean script fail. COUNT-BASIS WARNING, because an earlier draft of this note got it wrong: that 35 is files carrying ANY of the four `vendor_tokens`, which is the basis this gate actually enforces. A CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT-only sweep returns a much smaller number (16 at this change's base commit) and is NOT the figure to quote here — the earlier note said 16 while the table below listed 35 keys, which is the count-drift class this gate exists to catch. Re-derive from the table, never from a single-token grep. The root `scripts/` directory (this repo's own CI gates) is not listed here — it falls through to `unclassified_default`, which is also core, so it is ratcheted identically without needing a glob. loomwright/sdk-spike/* is listed EXPLICITLY even though it would already reach the same verdict via unclassified_default (core, allowance 0). The behaviour is identical; the message is not. Without the glob, the first person to add a reference there is told only that an unclassified path breached a default they have to go read about — a poor answer to 'why did CI fail?'. It is ratcheted rather than ADAPTER-exempt on purpose: the spike is an experimental Claude-Agent-SDK runner and therefore looks like an adapter, but it names NONE of the four vendor_tokens today (0 occurrences across 20 tracked files), so an exemption would grant a licence it has not earned and would silently absorb any future coupling. If it ever genuinely needs one of these tokens, that is a reviewable allowance raise like anywhere else. Note the class note's 'shell/python scripts' phrasing predates this entry: the spike is TypeScript, and CORE here means 'ratcheted, not exempt', not a statement about language.

allowances_note: Per-path measured baselines. A value is the count the gate itself measured on the commit that introduced or last raised it — never a hand-typed number. An entry for a path that does not exist, or for an ADAPTER-classified path, is an ERROR (the manifest stays self-cleaning, and an allowance cannot be used to quietly reclassify a file). A path absent from this map has an allowance of 0. TWO ENTRIES ARE NEW COUPLING INTRODUCED BY THE CHANGE THAT CREATED THIS FILE, and are called out rather than buried in the table: (1) `loomwright/docs/vendor-coupling-manifest.json` = 4, which is this file's own `vendor_tokens` declaration — the manifest is NOT exempted from its own scan, so adding a fifth token requires bumping this number in the same edit, which is the intended visibility rather than an inconvenience; (2) `loomwright/scripts/test-resolve-loomwright-root.sh` = 10, the resolver's self-test, which must name the harness variable literally in order to test the harness arm at all. It is deliberately CORE-with-an-allowance rather than ADAPTER: the resolver's exemption is justified by it being the single seam, and that argument does not extend to its test. Obfuscating those references so the counter could not see them would have been the dishonest alternative — it would lower the number without lowering the coupling. SELF-RAISE, recorded on purpose: this file's own allowance moved 4 -> 5 in the same edit that added a COUNT-BASIS WARNING to classes.core.note, because that warning names a vendor token literally in order to warn about it. That is the raise rule working as intended, not a loophole -- the manifest is scanned like anything else, so the cost of explaining the mechanism in prose is a visible, reviewable +1 rather than a silent exemption. It also answers the obvious question: there is NO deadlock. Adding a token raises this file's count by one and the allowance is bumped in the same edit, exactly as any other path would be. TWO ENTRIES ADDED 2026-09-02 by the agent_spawn payload probe (PR #170), both measured by `--print-allowances`, never hand-typed: `loomwright/scripts/capture-task-spawn-payload.sh` = 5 and `loomwright/docs/SPIKES/AGENT_SPAWN_PAYLOAD_PROBE.md` = 7. They are CORE and COUPLED respectively and are deliberately NOT adapter-exempted: the harness exists to observe the host tool's own hook payloads so it can never be vendor-neutral, but exempting it would make it invisible to this ratchet forever, whereas an allowance keeps it counted and puts any future reference in front of a reviewer. If the portability track later moves vendor-specific probes onto an adapter surface, these two entries are the ones to revisit. TWO ENTRIES ADDED 2026-09-02 by the statusline module (the `/setup statusline` item), both measured by `--print-allowances` and never hand-typed: `loomwright/scripts/setup-statusline.sh` = 2 and `loomwright/scripts/test-setup-statusline.sh` = 2. They are CORE and deliberately NOT adapter-exempted. The module writes the user-scope settings document, so the engine must name that path literally to have a default at all, and its self-test must name it to assert the write-containment case that proves the suite never touches the developers own file. Exempting either would make them invisible to this ratchet forever; an allowance keeps them counted and puts any future reference in front of a reviewer. NOTE ON THIS NOTE, which is the trap the prior self-raise recorded: this file is scanned against its own allowance, so an explanatory note that spelled the settings path literally would raise this entrys own count and trip the gate a second time, immediately after the first fix. It is therefore written WITHOUT the literal token — describing the path rather than quoting it — which is why no self-raise accompanies these two entries. If a future edit here needs to quote a token, bump this entry in the same edit rather than obfuscating the reference. THREE ENTRIES ADDED 2026-09-03 by the ui module (the `/setup ui` item — The Floor), all three measured by `--print-allowances` after staging every new file and never hand-typed: `loomwright/scripts/setup-ui.sh` = 3 (new, CORE), `loomwright/docs/FLOOR_UI.md` = 4 (new, COUPLED), and `loomwright/skills/setup/SKILL.md` 38 -> 40 (+2, COUPLED). They are deliberately NOT adapter-exempted. The module installs its bundle under a directory inside the user's host-tool config tree, so the engine must name that location literally to have a default at all, and both the module's registry row and its reference doc must name it to describe what the module writes and what `remove` takes away. Exempting any of the three would make them invisible to this ratchet forever; an allowance keeps them counted and puts any future reference in front of a reviewer. The BUNDLE (`loomwright/scripts/floor-ui/*`) and the self-test (`loomwright/scripts/test-setup-ui.sh`) hold NO entry and that is measured, not assumed: the page names no host-tool path at all, and every test case passes an explicit ui-directory override into a `mktemp -d`, which is also what proves the suite can never reach a developer's real config tree. As with the statusline entries directly above, this note DESCRIBES those paths rather than quoting them — spelling one literally here would raise this file's own entry and trip the gate a second time immediately after the first fix, which is the self-raise trap the earlier note recorded. If a future edit here needs to quote a token, bump this entry in the same edit rather than obfuscating the reference.
